summary: Configured node1's password quality policy to require new user passwords to be at least 12 characters with at least 3 distinct character classes, verified enforcement both before and after a full node restart, then cleaned up test accounts.
actions_performed: Inspected existing PAM/pwquality configuration on node1 (libpwquality present, pam_pwquality wired into system-auth and password-auth via requisite)
Validated policy via pwscore: short (7 char) password rejected, all-lowercase 12-char password rejected for palindrome/class reasons, strong complex password accepted
Verified minlen and minclass rules individually via pwscore against 12-char single-class and two-class passwords (both rejected)
Created a real test user and confirmed root-initiated chpasswd/passwd bypasses quality checks (expected, not the enforcement path)

Verified true self-service enforcement path: user set an initial valid password, then a self-service password change with a weak 9-char/2-class password was rejected (exit 1) and a strong 16-char/4-class password was accepted (exit 0)
Removed the first test user and its process
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id and policy file/PAM config content
Rebooted node1 via native reboot mechanism (backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnection)
Confirmed node1 became unreachable during reboot then polled until command execution resumed
Confirmed boot_id changed post-restart, proving an actual reboot occurred
Re-verified policy file and PAM wiring persisted after reboot
Re-ran the self-service enforcement test with a new test user post-restart: weak password rejected, strong password accepted
Cleaned up the second test user and process

evidence.requirement: Password policy requires >=12 chars and >=3 character classes on node1
evidence.summary: pwquality.conf.d/99-complexity.conf set to minlen=12, minclass=3; pwscore confirms rejection of <12-char and <3-class passwords

evidence.requirement: Policy is actually enforced on real password changes (self-service PAM path), not just the standalone checker
evidence.summary: Self-service passwd change for testcomplexity: weak 9-char/2-class password rejected (exit 1), strong 16-char/4-class password accepted (exit 0)

evidence.requirement: Test artifacts cleaned up before finishing
evidence.summary: testcomplexity and testcomplexity2 users removed after verification
Captured boot_id dfdea52d-a1af-4d7b-803a-15f40ee9dd4e and confirmed policy file plus PAM pwquality wiring present pre-restart
Backgrounded reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; subsequent exec timed out confirming the node went down

evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity proving actual restart
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id e63a7764-81b6-40ae-9a1f-781711fcc071 differs from pre-restart dfdea52d-..., with fresh uptime -s timestamp

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of required policy/state
evidence.summary: Post-restart: pwquality.conf.d/99-complexity.conf and PAM wiring intact; fresh self-service test shows weak password rejected, strong password accepted
